request: We are an IT services company with about $12M in ARR and $2M in cash, and I have to choose our main move for the next twelve months. The options I see: keep the current plan, put part of engineering on technical debt, hire engineers, reserve GPU capacity on a second cloud, or raise list prices by 8%. I watch cash at year end, client churn, runway, availability against our SLA, and NPS. I worry about a price war, a GPU shortage, a big client leaving, clients changing their requirements, a hard hiring market, a cash squeeze, a market downturn and a payroll tax rise from July. Which move gives us the best year?

qa.q: How many engineers would you hire?
What matters most when you compare the moves?
qa.a: Cash at year end and client churn first, availability next, runway and NPS least.

author: LW-E01
reviewEdits: Kept every lever start at the fork date, October 2026.
Chose to judge the forks on the average with a margin, not on the worst case.
Left the eight world hypotheses off: they are layers to switch on.
